definition: A relationship $y = kx$ with $k$ constant: doubling $x$ doubles $y$, and the graph is a straight line through the origin.
A relationship $y = \frac{k}{x}$ with $k$ constant: doubling $x$ halves $y$, so the product $xy$ stays the same.
A trend between two variables, positive when one tends to rise as the other rises and negative when it tends to fall; it does not by itself show that one causes the other.
A single straight line or smooth curve drawn through the trend of plotted data, with the points scattered as evenly as possible on both sides.
A line through a plotted point reaching one absolute uncertainty either side of it, showing the range in which the true value could lie.
Choosing what to plot on each axis, from a theoretical equation, so that the predicted relationship gives a straight-line graph of the form $y = mx + c$.
An axis on which equal distances stand for equal factors, usually powers of ten, so values spanning many orders of magnitude fit on one graph.
